subproblem.title: Gram-determinant lower bound c^k ≤ √det(⟨Te_i, Te_j⟩) for a linear map with |Ts| ≥ c|s| (Jacobian bound of step 6a)
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let T : ℝ^k → ℝ^P be a continuous linear map (ℝ^m = Eucl m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)), and let c ≥ 0 satisfy c|s| ≤ |Ts| for every s ∈ ℝ^k. Let e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin k) and let G := (⟨Te_i, Te_j⟩)_{i,j} be the k×k Gram matrix (Matrix.of). Then c^k ≤ √det G.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (T : Eucl k →L[ℝ] Eucl P) (c : ℝ), 0 ≤ c → (∀ s : Eucl k, c * ‖s‖ ≤ ‖T s‖) → c ^ k ≤ Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (T (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (T (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))).det
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the Jacobian bound of step (6a) of the parent proof ("the Gram matrix (⟨∂_aΦ(w), ∂_bΦ(w)⟩)_{a,b} is ≥ c²·I, so JΦ(w) ≥ c^k > 0"), isolated for one linear map T. In the parent T = DΦ(w), and the hypothesis |DΦ(w)s| ≥ c|s| is supplied by the sibling fderiv_lower_bound.

Conventions. ℝ^m = Eucl m with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|. e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^k, and x = Σ_i x_i e_i for x ∈ ℝ^k. G_{ij} = ⟨Te_i, Te_j⟩.

1. (Symmetry.) G_{ij} = ⟨Te_i, Te_j⟩ = ⟨Te_j, Te_i⟩ = G_{ji} (real_inner_comm). So the real matrix G is Hermitian: Gᴴ = Gᵀ = G (Matrix.IsHermitian).
2. (Quadratic form.) For x ∈ ℝ^k with coordinates (x_i):
 Σ_i x_i Σ_j G_{ij} x_j = Σ_{i,j} x_i x_j ⟨Te_i, Te_j⟩ = ⟨Σ_i x_i Te_i, Σ_j x_j Te_j⟩ = ⟨Tx, Tx⟩ = |Tx|².
 This uses Tx = Σ_i x_i Te_i (linearity of T) and bilinearity of the real inner product. In matrix notation xᵀGx = |Tx|² (dotProduct x (G.mulVec x)).
3. (Eigenvalues ≥ c².) By the spectral theorem for Hermitian matrices (Mathlib Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvectorBasis, Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues) there is an orthonormal basis u_0, …, u_{k−1} of ℝ^k with Gu_i = λ_i u_i. Moreover λ_i = u_iᵀGu_i (Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues_eq; star and re are the identity on ℝ).
 - By step 2, λ_i = |Tu_i|².
 - By the hypothesis with s = u_i and |u_i| = 1: 0 ≤ c = c|u_i| ≤ |Tu_i|. Hence λ_i = |Tu_i|² ≥ c².
4. (Determinant.) det G = Π_i λ_i (Matrix.IsHermitian.det_eq_prod_eigenvalues). Since 0 ≤ c² ≤ λ_i for every i, Π_i λ_i ≥ Π_i c² = (c²)^k (Finset.prod_le_prod₀).
5. (Square root.) Because c ≥ 0, c^k = √((c^k)²) = √((c²)^k) ≤ √det G, by monotonicity of the square root. ∎

Edge cases are covered by the same argument:
 - k = 0: the matrix is empty, det G = 1 and c^0 = 1 = √1 (empty products in steps 3–4).
 - k > P: T has a nontrivial kernel, so the hypothesis forces c = 0, and step 5 gives 0 ≤ √det G.

Tactic script:
  intro P k T c hc hT
  set G : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ := Matrix.of fun i j =>
    inner ℝ (T (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (T (EuclideanSpace.single j 1)) with hG
  have hHerm : Matrix.IsHermitian G := by
    ext i j
    simp [hG, Matrix.conjTranspose_apply, real_inner_comm]
  -- the quadratic form of G is |T x|²
  have hquad : ∀ x : Eucl k, dotProduct (⇑x : Fin k → ℝ) (Matrix.mulVec G (⇑x : Fin k → ℝ)) = ‖T x‖ ^ 2 := by
    intro x
    have hx : x = ∑ i, x i • EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ) := by
      conv_lhs => rw [← (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin k) ℝ).sum_repr x]
      simp
    rw [← real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq]
    conv_rhs => rw [hx]
    simp only [map_sum, map_smul, inner_sum, sum_inner, inner_smul_left, inner_smul_right,
      Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, hG, Matrix.of_apply, conj_trivial]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
    congr 1
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => ?_
    rw [real_inner_comm]
    ring
  have heig : ∀ i, c ^ 2 ≤ hHerm.eigenvalues i := by
    intro i
    rw [hHerm.eigenvalues_eq i]
    set u : Eucl k := hHerm.eigenvectorBasis i with hu
    have hun : ‖u‖ = 1 := (hHerm.eigenvectorBasis).orthonormal.1 i
    have h1 := hquad u
    simp only [star_trivial, RCLike.re_to_real]
    rw [h1]
    have h2 := hT u
    rw [hun, mul_one] at h2
    nlinarith [norm_nonneg (T u)]
  have hdet : Matrix.det G = ∏ i, hHerm.eigenvalues i := by
    simpa using hHerm.det_eq_prod_eigenvalues
  have hprod : (c ^ 2) ^ k ≤ Matrix.det G := by
    rw [hdet]
    calc (c ^ 2) ^ k = ∏ _i : Fin k, c ^ 2 := by simp
      _ ≤ ∏ i, hHerm.eigenvalues i :=
          Finset.prod_le_prod₀ (fun _ _ => sq_nonneg c) (fun i _ => heig i)
  calc c ^ k = Real.sqrt ((c ^ k) ^ 2) := (Real.sqrt_sq (pow_nonneg hc k)).symm
    _ = Real.sqrt ((c ^ 2) ^ k) := by ring_nf
    _ ≤ Real.sqrt (Matrix.det G) := Real.sqrt_le_sqrt hprod

Spectral theorem: for the orthonormal eigenbasis u_i, λ_i = u_iᵀGu_i = |Tu_i|² ≥ c².
det G = Π_i λ_i ≥ (c²)^k (prod_le_prod₀), hence c^k = √((c²)^k) ≤ √det G.

subproblem.title: Measurability and tangential bound Λ^k‖β‖θ of push-forward integrands θ·(A_#ξ)(β) on a rectifiable triple (steps 2–3)
subproblem.statement: Let P, Q, k ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and let (M, θ, ξ) satisfy IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ (H^k = μHE[k] on ℝ^P). Let A : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q), β : ℝ^P → Covector(ℝ^Q, k) and Λ ∈ ℝ. Assume that x ↦ A(x)_#ξ(x) (A_# = nVectorPushforward k A) and β are a.e.-strongly measurable for H^k⌞M. Assume also that for H^k-a.e. x ∈ M, |A(x)v| ≤ Λ|v| for every v in every weighted approximate tangent space T_x of (M, θ) at x. Then x ↦ θ(x)·(A(x)_#ξ(x))(β(x)) is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^k⌞M, and |θ(x)·(A(x)_#ξ(x))(β(x))| ≤ Λ^k·‖β(x)‖·θ(x) for H^k-a.e. x ∈ M, where ‖β(x)‖ is the operator norm of the covector β(x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q k : ℕ) (U M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) k) (A : Eucl P → (Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl Q)) (β : Eucl P → Covector (Eucl Q) k) (Λ : ℝ), IsOpen U → IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ → AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => nVectorPushforward k (A x) (ξ x)) ((μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M) → AEStronglyMeasurable β ((μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M) → (∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), ∀ Tx : Submodule ℝ (Eucl P), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x Tx → ∀ v ∈ Tx, ‖A x v‖ ≤ Λ * ‖v‖) → AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => θ x * nVectorPushforward k (A x) (ξ x) (β x)) ((μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M) ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), |θ x * nVectorPushforward k (A x) (ξ x) (β x)| ≤ Λ ^ k * ‖β x‖ * θ x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2 and 3 of the parent proof (the single dominator, and the measurability of F_j and F), separated from the choice of A. In the parent the lemma is applied twice.
 - A = Dg_j, β = ω∘g_j: |Dg_j(x)v| ≤ Λ′|v| because g_j is Λ′-Lipschitz; measurability of x ↦ Dg_j(x)_#ξ(x) comes from the parent's sibling pushforward_measurable with f = g_j, L = Dg_j.
 - A = L, β = ω∘g: |L(x)v| ≤ Λ|v| on weighted tangent spaces, because t ↦ g(x + tv) is Λ|v|-Lipschitz with derivative L(x)v at 0; measurability again from pushforward_measurable.

Conventions. H := μHE[k] on ℝ^P. Covectors and k-vectors carry operator norms, and |γ(u_0, …, u_{k−1})| ≤ ‖γ‖·Π_a|u_a| for a k-covector γ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm).

1. (θ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H⌞M.) For q ∈ ℕ let K_q := {x : |x| ≤ q} ∖ thickening(1/(q+1), ℝ^P ∖ U), where thickening(r, E) = {x : dist(x, z) < r for some z ∈ E} is open.
 - K_q is closed and bounded, hence compact.
 - K_q ⊆ U: a point x ∉ U lies in ℝ^P ∖ U ⊆ thickening(1/(q+1), ℝ^P ∖ U).
 - U ⊆ ⋃_q K_q: for x ∈ U choose ε > 0 with B(x, ε) ⊆ U (U is open) and q ∈ ℕ with q ≥ |x| and 1/(q+1) < ε. If x were in thickening(1/(q+1), ℝ^P ∖ U), some z ∉ U would satisfy |x − z| < 1/(q+1) < ε, i.e. z ∈ B(x, ε) ⊆ U, a contradiction. So x ∈ K_q.
 Since M ⊆ U (field subset), M = ⋃_q (M ∩ K_q). By the field integrableOn of the triple, θ is H-integrable, in particular a.e.-strongly measurable, on each M ∩ K_q. For a countable union this gives that θ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H⌞M (aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff).
2. (Measurability of the integrand.) The evaluation map NVector(ℝ^Q, k) × Covector(ℝ^Q, k) → ℝ, (N, γ) ↦ N(γ), is bounded bilinear, hence continuous (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply). Composing it with the a.e.-strongly measurable map x ↦ (A(x)_#ξ(x), β(x)) (AEStronglyMeasurable.prodMk) gives an a.e.-strongly measurable function. Its product with θ (step 1) is a.e.-strongly measurable for H⌞M. This is the first conclusion.
3. (Good points.) For H⌞M-a.e. x the following hold simultaneously:
 - x ∈ M (ae_restrict_mem₀; M is null-measurable);
 - the orientation clause of the triple gives an orthonormal τ : Fin k → ℝ^P such that span τ is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at x and ξ(x) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(x) = −simpleNVector τ;

subproblem.title: Dominated convergence of set integrals along a countable partition (countable additivity and Tannery's theorem; steps 5 and 7)
subproblem.statement: Let (X, μ) be a measure space, let S ⊆ X, and let (E_i)_{i∈ℕ} be pairwise disjoint μ-null-measurable subsets of X with S = ⋃_i E_i μ-almost everywhere. Let G : X → ℝ be μ-integrable on S, and let f_j : X → ℝ (j ∈ ℕ) and f₀ : X → ℝ be a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞S. Assume that |f_j| ≤ G μ⌞S-a.e. for all sufficiently large j, that |f₀| ≤ G μ⌞S-a.e., and that ∫_{E_i} f_j dμ → ∫_{E_i} f₀ dμ as j → ∞ for every i. Then ∫_S f_j dμ → ∫_S f₀ dμ as j → ∞.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] (μ : Measure X) (S : Set X) (E : ℕ → Set X) (f : ℕ → X → ℝ) (f₀ G : X → ℝ), (∀ i, NullMeasurableSet (E i) μ) → Pairwise (Function.onFun Disjoint E) → S =ᵐ[μ] (⋃ i, E i) → IntegrableOn G S μ → (∀ j, AEStronglyMeasurable (f j) (μ.restrict S)) → AEStronglyMeasurable f₀ (μ.restrict S) → (∀ᶠ j in atTop, ∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict S), |f j x| ≤ G x) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict S), |f₀ x| ≤ G x) → (∀ i, Tendsto (fun j => ∫ x in E i, f j x ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x in E i, f₀ x ∂μ))) → Tendsto (fun j => ∫ x in S, f j x ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x in S, f₀ x ∂μ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5 and 7 of the parent proof (countable additivity over the chart pieces, and dominated convergence for series), stated for an abstract measure space. In the parent: X = ℝ^P, μ = μHE[k], S = M, E_i = the disjointed chart pieces, f_j = F_j, f₀ = F, and G = max(Λ, Λ′)^k·sup‖ω‖·1_{g⁻¹(K)}·θ.

Write S′ := ⋃_i E_i.
1. (Same restricted measure.) Since S = S′ μ-a.e., μ⌞S = μ⌞S′ (Measure.restrict_congr_set), and ∫_S φ dμ = ∫_{S′} φ dμ for every φ (setIntegral_congr_set). In particular G is μ-integrable on S′.
2. (Integrability.) For every j in the eventual range of the bound, f_j is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞S = μ⌞S′ and |f_j| ≤ G a.e. So f_j is μ-integrable on S′ (Integrable.mono'). Likewise f₀ is μ-integrable on S′.
3. (Countable additivity.) The E_i are null-measurable and pairwise disjoint, hence pairwise a.e.-disjoint. For φ integrable on S′, ∫_{S′} φ dμ = Σ_i ∫_{E_i} φ dμ (integral_iUnion_ae). Write a_i(j) := ∫_{E_i} f_j dμ and a_i := ∫_{E_i} f₀ dμ. With steps 1–2:
 - ∫_S f_j dμ = Σ_i a_i(j) for all large j;
 - ∫_S f₀ dμ = Σ_i a_i.
4. (Summable domination.) Let b_i := ∫_{E_i} G dμ. Since G is integrable on S′, Σ_i b_i converges, to ∫_{S′} G dμ (hasSum_integral_iUnion_ae). For each i, μ⌞E_i ≤ μ⌞S′ = μ⌞S (E_i ⊆ S′). So for all large j, |f_j| ≤ G μ⌞E_i-a.e., and |a_i(j)| ≤ b_i (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le, with G integrable on E_i).
5. (Tannery.) We have: a_i(j) → a_i for every i (hypothesis); |a_i(j)| ≤ b_i for every i and all large j; and Σ_i b_i < ∞. By dominated convergence for series (Tannery's theorem; Mathlib tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence), Σ_i a_i(j) → Σ_i a_i. By step 3 and eventual equality (Tendsto.congr'), ∫_S f_j dμ → ∫_S f₀ dμ. ∎

subproblem.title: Measurable relative orientation on a C¹ antilipschitz chart: JΦ·ξ(Φ) = σ·simpleNVector(∂Φ) with σ = ±1 (step 6c)
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and let (M, θ, ξ) satisfy IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ (H^k = μHE[k] on ℝ^P). Let Φ : ℝ^k → ℝ^P be C¹ and c-antilipschitz on an open set Ω ⊆ ℝ^k for some c > 0. Write ∂_bΦ(w) := DΦ(w)e_b (DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w, e_b = EuclideanSpace.single b 1), ∂Φ(w) := (∂_0Φ(w), …, ∂_{k−1}Φ(w)) and JΦ(w) := √det(⟨∂_aΦ(w), ∂_bΦ(w)⟩)_{a,b}. Then there is σ : ℝ^k → ℝ, a.e.-strongly measurable for L^k⌞(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M)) (L^k = volume), such that for L^k-a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M): σ(w) ∈ {1, −1} and JΦ(w)·ξ(Φ(w)) = σ(w)·simpleNVector(∂Φ(w)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) k) (Φ : Eucl k → Eucl P) (Ω : Set (Eucl k)), IsOpen U → IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ → IsOpen Ω → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → ∃ σ : Eucl k → ℝ, AEStronglyMeasurable σ ((volume : Measure (Eucl k)).restrict (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' M)) ∧ ∀ᵐ w ∂((volume : Measure (Eucl k)).restrict (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' M)), (σ w = 1 ∨ σ w = -1) ∧ Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))).det • ξ (Φ w) = σ w • simpleNVector (fun b => fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single b 1))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step (6c) of the parent proof, together with the measurability of the sign claimed in (6d), for a triple on an arbitrary open U. The parent's ingredients are: good parameters; ξ(x) = ε·simpleNVector τ with span τ = range DΦ(w); simpleNVector(∂Φ(w)) = det B·simpleNVector τ; |det B| = JΦ(w); and the sign built from the covector β_w with β_w(∂Φ(w)) = JΦ(w)². Two harmless changes are made:
 - the sign is σ(w) := 1 if ξ(Φ(w))(β_w) ≥ 0 and σ(w) := −1 otherwise, so σ is ±1 everywhere and no division by JΦ is needed;
 - β_w is written as the pull-back of one fixed covector, which makes w ↦ β_w visibly continuous.

Conventions. H := μHE[k] on ℝ^P; L := volume on ℝ^k; S := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M). For a k-vector N and a k-covector γ, N(γ) is the pairing; simpleNVector v (γ) = γ(v); covectorPullback k A γ = γ(A·, …, A·). † is the Hilbert-space adjoint (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint), and ‖·‖ on k-vectors is the operator norm.

1. (A Borel representative of ξ.) ξ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H⌞M (field aestronglyMeasurable of the triple). Fix a strongly measurable ξ̃ with ξ = ξ̃ H⌞M-a.e. (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk).
2. (Good points of M ∩ Φ(Ω).) For H⌞(M ∩ Φ(Ω))-a.e. y, the following three statements hold.
 (a) For every w ∈ Ω with Φ(w) = y, range DΦ(w) is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at y. This is the sibling weighted_tangent_on_c1_chart with V := U. Its hypotheses hold: U is open; M ⊆ U, M is H-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M, and θ is H-integrable on M ∩ K for compact K ⊆ U (the fields subset, nullMeasurableSet, pos and integrableOn of the triple); Ω is open and Φ is C¹ and antilipschitz on Ω.
 (b) There is an orthonormal τ : Fin k → ℝ^P such that span τ is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at y and ξ(y) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(y) = −simpleNVector τ. This is the field orients, an H⌞M-a.e. statement, restricted to M ∩ Φ(Ω) ⊆ M (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset).
 (c) ξ(y) = ξ̃(y), by step 1 restricted in the same way.
3. (Pull-back to parameters.) Apply the sibling ae_pullback to M, Φ, Ω and the property p(y) := (a) ∧ (b) ∧ (c). Its hypotheses hold: Ω is measurable (open), Φ is measurable (continuous), Φ is antilipschitz on Ω, and M is H-null-measurable. Hence S is L-null-measurable and p(Φ(w)) holds for L⌞S-a.e. w. Moreover L⌞S-a.e. w lies in S (ae_restrict_mem₀).
4. (The test covector.) Let β₀ := wedgeCovectors k (a ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj a), a k-covector on ℝ^k. Let β_w := covectorPullback k (DΦ(w)†) β₀, a k-covector on ℝ^P.
 - Formula. By wedgeCovectors_apply_det, for u = (u_0, …, u_{k−1}) in ℝ^P:
  β_w(u) = det(proj_a(DΦ(w)†u_b))_{a,b} = det(⟨e_a, DΦ(w)†u_b⟩)_{a,b} = det(⟨DΦ(w)e_a, u_b⟩)_{a,b}
  (EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left, adjoint_inner_right). In particular β_w(∂Φ(w)) = det(⟨∂_aΦ(w), ∂_bΦ(w)⟩)_{a,b} =: Δ(w).
 - Continuity of w ↦ β_w. w ↦ DΦ(w) is continuous because Φ is C¹ (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv); the adjoint is a linear isometry; A ↦ covectorPullback k A is continuous (it is ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM, continuous by ContinuousAlternatingMap.continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM); and evaluating a continuous linear map at the fixed β₀ is continuous.
5. (The sign and its measurability.) Put p(w) := ξ(Φ(w))(β_w). Put σ(w) := 1 if p(w) ≥ 0 and σ(w) := −1 if p(w) < 0; so σ(w) ∈ {1, −1} for every w.
 - By step 3(c), w ↦ ξ(Φ(w)) agrees L⌞S-a.e. with w ↦ ξ̃(Φ(w)), which is strongly measurable (ξ̃ strongly measurable, Φ measurable). So it is a.e.-strongly measurable for L⌞S.
 - The pairing (N, γ) ↦ N(γ) is bounded bilinear, hence continuous, on NVector × Covector (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply). With step 4, p is a.e.-strongly measurable for L⌞S.
 - σ = s∘p with the Borel function s(t) = 1 (t ≥ 0), s(t) = −1 (t < 0). So σ is a.e.-measurable, hence a.e.-strongly measurable, for L⌞S.
6. (The identity at good parameters.) Fix w ∈ S at which p(Φ(w)) holds; this is L⌞S-a.e. by step 3. Let x := Φ(w) and v := ∂Φ(w), and let τ be as in 2(b).
 (6.1) θ(x) > 0 since x ∈ M. By 2(a) (with this w) and 2(b), range DΦ(w) and span τ are both weighted approximate tangent spaces of (M, θ) at x. So they are equal (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique, which needs θ(x) ≠ 0).
 (6.2) Each v_b = DΦ(w)e_b lies in range DΦ(w) = span τ. So v_b = Σ_a c_a τ_a for some coefficients (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun), and pairing with τ_a gives c_a = ⟨τ_a, v_b⟩ by orthonormality (Orthonormal.inner_right_fintype). Let B be the k×k matrix B_{ba} := ⟨τ_a, v_b⟩ (Matrix.of); then v_b = Σ_a B_{ba} τ_a. The second identity of the sibling simple_nvector_algebra gives simpleNVector v = d·simpleNVector τ, where d := det B.
 (6.3) Norms. The first identity of simple_nvector_algebra for τ gives ‖simpleNVector τ‖² = det(⟨τ_a, τ_b⟩) = det I = 1, so ‖simpleNVector τ‖ = 1 (norms are ≥ 0). Hence ‖simpleNVector v‖ = |d|·‖simpleNVector τ‖ = |d|. For k-vectors use the operator-norm inequality ‖r·N‖ ≤ |r|·‖N‖ twice, with r = d and r = d⁻¹; the case d = 0 is direct.
 - The first identity for v gives Δ(w) = ‖simpleNVector v‖² = d². So JΦ(w) = √(d²) = |d|.
 - By step 4, simpleNVector v (β_w) = β_w(v) = Δ(w) = d².
 (6.4) If d = 0, then JΦ(w) = 0 and simpleNVector v = 0. So both sides of JΦ(w)·ξ(x) = σ(w)·simpleNVector v are 0.
 (6.5) If d ≠ 0: from simpleNVector v = d·simpleNVector τ and (6.3), d·simpleNVector τ(β_w) = d². Hence simpleNVector τ(β_w) = d.
  - If ξ(x) = simpleNVector τ, then p(w) = d. So σ(w) = 1 when d > 0 and σ(w) = −1 when d < 0; in both cases |d| = σ(w)·d. Therefore JΦ(w)·ξ(x) = |d|·simpleNVector τ = σ(w)·d·simpleNVector τ = σ(w)·simpleNVector v.
  - If ξ(x) = −simpleNVector τ, then p(w) = −d. So σ(w) = 1 when d < 0 and σ(w) = −1 when d > 0; in both cases −|d| = σ(w)·d. Therefore JΦ(w)·ξ(x) = −|d|·simpleNVector τ = σ(w)·d·simpleNVector τ = σ(w)·simpleNVector v.
 Thus σ(w) ∈ {1, −1} and JΦ(w)·ξ(Φ(w)) = σ(w)·simpleNVector(∂Φ(w)) for L⌞S-a.e. w. Together with step 5 this is the assertion. ∎
 For k = 0 every step holds verbatim: Fin 0-families are empty, B is the empty matrix with det B = 1, and JΦ ≡ 1.

subproblem.title: Signed change of variables ∫_A h dH^k = ∫_{Ω∩Φ⁻¹(A)} h(Φ)·JΦ dL^k through an injective Lipschitz–antilipschitz chart (step 6b(β))
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let Ω ⊆ ℝ^k be open, and let Φ : ℝ^k → ℝ^P be Lipschitz on Ω and c-antilipschitz on Ω for some c > 0 (c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω). Let A ⊆ Φ(Ω) be H^k-null-measurable (H^k = μHE[k] on ℝ^P), and let h : ℝ^P → ℝ be H^k-integrable on A. Put D := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A) and JΦ(w) := √det(⟨DΦ(w)e_i, DΦ(w)e_j⟩)_{i,j}, where DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w and e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1. Then w ↦ h(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) is L^k-integrable on D (L^k = volume), and ∫_A h dH^k = ∫_D h(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) dL^k(w).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl k → Eucl P) (Ω : Set (Eucl k)) (A : Set (Eucl P)) (h : Eucl P → ℝ), IsOpen Ω → (∃ K : ℝ≥0, LipschitzOnWith K Φ Ω) → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → A ⊆ Φ '' Ω → NullMeasurableSet A (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl P)) → IntegrableOn h A (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl P)) → IntegrableOn (fun w => h (Φ w) * Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))).det) (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' A) (volume : Measure (Eucl k)) ∧ ∫ x in A, h x ∂(μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl P)) = ∫ w in Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' A, h (Φ w) * Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))).det ∂(volume : Measure (Eucl k))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step (6b)(β) of the parent proof ("applying the formula to the positive and negative parts … gives … w ↦ φ(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) is L^k⌞D-integrable with ∫_{G_K} φ dH = ∫_D φ(Φ(w))·JΦ(w) dw"). It is stated here for an arbitrary integrable real h and an arbitrary null-measurable A ⊆ Φ(Ω). The parent's implementation remark is followed literally: the signed formula comes from the lintegral identity of chart_change_of_variables applied to ENNReal.ofReal of the positive and negative parts.

Conventions. H := μHE[k] on ℝ^P; L := volume on ℝ^k; J := JΦ; ofReal := ENNReal.ofReal; ‖t‖ₑ = ofReal|t| for t ∈ ℝ; ∫⁻ is the [0,∞]-valued integral.

1. (J is nonnegative and Borel.) J ≥ 0, being a square root. J is Borel measurable:
 - w ↦ DΦ(w) is Borel measurable for every Φ (Mathlib measurable_fderiv);
 - hence so are the columns w ↦ DΦ(w)e_i (evaluation at e_i is continuous linear);
 - the entries ⟨DΦ(w)e_i, DΦ(w)e_j⟩ are measurable (the inner product is continuous);
 - the determinant is a polynomial, hence continuous, function of the entries, and √ is continuous.
2. (The sibling chart_change_of_variables.) Its hypotheses hold for (Φ, Ω, A): Ω is open, Φ is Lipschitz and c-antilipschitz on Ω, A ⊆ Φ(Ω), and A is H-null-measurable. Since h is integrable, hence a.e.-measurable, for H⌞A, the following are a.e.-measurable for H⌞A: g₊ := ofReal∘h, g₋ := ofReal∘(−h) and g₀ := ‖h‖ₑ. The sibling gives:
 - D is L-null-measurable;
 - g₊∘Φ and g₋∘Φ are a.e.-measurable for L⌞D;
 - for g ∈ {g₊, g₋, g₀}: ∫⁻_A g dH = ∫⁻_D g(Φ(w))·ofReal(J(w)) dw.
3. (Measurability on D.) For every real t, t = toReal(ofReal t) − toReal(ofReal(−t)), since one of the two terms is 0. Hence h∘Φ = toReal∘(g₊∘Φ) − toReal∘(g₋∘Φ) is a.e.-measurable for L⌞D. So F(w) := h(Φ(w))·J(w) is a.e.-strongly measurable for L⌞D, as a product with the measurable J.
4. (Integrability on D.) Since J ≥ 0, ‖F(w)‖ₑ = ‖h(Φ(w))‖ₑ·ofReal(J(w)). By step 2 with g₀, ∫⁻_D ‖F‖ₑ dL = ∫⁻_A ‖h‖ₑ dH < ∞, because h is integrable on A. With step 3, F is L-integrable on D. This is the first conclusion.
5. (The identity.) For a real function f integrable for a measure ν,
 ∫ f dν = toReal(∫⁻ ofReal(f) dν) − toReal(∫⁻ ofReal(−f) dν)
 (Mathlib integral_eq_lintegral_pos_part_sub_lintegral_neg_part). Apply this to h on (A, H) and to F on (D, L) (step 4):
 ∫_A h dH = toReal(∫⁻_A ofReal(h) dH) − toReal(∫⁻_A ofReal(−h) dH)
  = toReal(∫⁻_D ofReal(h(Φ w))·ofReal(J w) dw) − toReal(∫⁻_D ofReal(−h(Φ w))·ofReal(J w) dw)   (step 2)
  = toReal(∫⁻_D ofReal(F(w)) dw) − toReal(∫⁻_D ofReal(−F(w)) dw) = ∫_D F dL.
 The third equality uses ofReal(a)·ofReal(b) = ofReal(a·b) for b = J(w) ≥ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_mul') and −h(Φ w)·J(w) = −F(w). This is the second conclusion. ∎

subproblem.title: Chart representation of push-forward integrals by one L¹ weight ψ: ∫_G θ(A_#ξ)(α∘f) dH^k = ∫_Ω ψ·α(f∘Φ)(∂(f∘Φ)) (steps 6a–6d)
subproblem.statement: Let P, Q, k ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and let (M, θ, ξ) satisfy IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ (H^k = μHE[k] on ℝ^P). Let Φ : ℝ^k → ℝ^P be C¹, let Ω ⊆ ℝ^k be open, and let Φ be Lipschitz on Ω and c-antilipschitz on Ω for some c > 0. Let G ⊆ ℝ^P be H^k-null-measurable with G ⊆ M and G ⊆ Φ(Ω), and with θ H^k-integrable on G. Then there is ψ : ℝ^k → ℝ, Lebesgue integrable on Ω, with the following property. Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q, A : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q) and α : ℝ^Q → Covector(ℝ^Q, k) be such that (i) f∘Φ has Fréchet derivative A(Φ(w))∘DΦ(w) at L^k-a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(G), and (ii) x ↦ θ(x)·(A(x)_#ξ(x))(α(f(x))) is H^k-integrable on G. Then ∫_G θ(x)·(A(x)_#ξ(x))(α(f(x))) dH^k(x) = ∫_Ω ψ(w)·α(f(Φ(w)))(∂_0(f∘Φ)(w), …, ∂_{k−1}(f∘Φ)(w)) dw. Here A_# = nVectorPushforward k A, DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w and ∂_b(f∘Φ)(w) = fderiv ℝ (f∘Φ) w e_b with e_b = EuclideanSpace.single b 1.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps (6a)–(6d) of the parent proof for one chart, with G := G_K, treating the two integrands at once. About the pair (A, f), (6c)–(6d) only use two facts: (A(x)_#ξ(x))(α(f(x))) is evaluated through ξ(x) = s·JΦ⁻¹·simpleNVector(∂Φ(w)), and A(Φ(w))∂_bΦ(w) = ∂_b(f∘Φ)(w). In the parent this is applied with (f, A) = (g_j, Dg_j) (C¹ chain rule) and with (f, A) = (g, L) (sibling chart_chain_rule). The weight ψ = 1_D·(θ∘Φ)·σ does not depend on (f, A, α).

Conventions. H := μHE[k] on ℝ^P; L := volume on ℝ^k; J := JΦ = √det(⟨DΦ(w)e_a, DΦ(w)e_b⟩)_{a,b}; D := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(G); ∂Φ(w) := (DΦ(w)e_b)_b; ofReal := ENNReal.ofReal.

1. (Sets.) D ⊆ Ω, and D ⊆ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) because G ⊆ M.
2. (Jacobian bound, (6a).) Let w ∈ Ω. Φ is differentiable at w (C¹). The sibling fderiv_lower_bound gives c|s| ≤ |DΦ(w)s| for all s. The sibling gram_det_lower_bound with T := DΦ(w) then gives c^k ≤ J(w). In particular J(w) ≥ c^k > 0 on Ω.
3. (Orientation, (6c).) The sibling chart_orientation applies (U open, the triple, Ω open, Φ C¹ and antilipschitz on Ω). It gives σ : ℝ^k → ℝ, a.e.-strongly measurable for L⌞(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M)), with σ(w) = ±1 and J(w)·ξ(Φ(w)) = σ(w)·simpleNVector(∂Φ(w)) for L⌞(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M))-a.e. w. By step 1 both facts hold for L⌞D (restriction to a subset: ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset, and AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure with Measure.restrict_mono).
4. (θ on the chart, (6b).) θ is H-integrable on G, so ofReal∘θ is a.e.-measurable for H⌞G. The sibling chart_change_of_variables applies (Ω open, Φ Lipschitz and c-antilipschitz on Ω, G ⊆ Φ(Ω), G null-measurable). It gives:
 - D is L-null-measurable;
 - w ↦ ofReal(θ(Φ(w))) is a.e.-measurable for L⌞D;
 - ∫⁻_G ofReal(θ) dH = ∫⁻_D ofReal(θ(Φ(w)))·ofReal(J(w)) dw.
 For w ∈ D, Φ(w) ∈ G ⊆ M, so θ(Φ(w)) > 0 and θ(Φ(w)) = toReal(ofReal(θ(Φ(w)))). As L⌞D-a.e. w lies in D (ae_restrict_mem₀), θ∘Φ is a.e.-measurable for L⌞D.
5. (The weight.) Put F₁(w) := θ(Φ(w))·σ(w) and ψ := 1_D·F₁ (ψ = F₁ on D and 0 elsewhere). F₁ is a.e.-strongly measurable for L⌞D by steps 3–4. D is null-measurable for L⌞Ω, and (L⌞Ω)⌞D = L⌞(D ∩ Ω) = L⌞D (Measure.restrict_restrict₀ and D ⊆ Ω). So ψ is a.e.-strongly measurable for L⌞Ω (aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff₀).
6. (ψ ∈ L¹(Ω), (6d).) ∫⁻_Ω |ψ| dL = ∫⁻_D |F₁| dL (lintegral_indicator₀ and step 5). For L⌞D-a.e. w we have |σ(w)| = 1 and θ(Φ(w)) > 0, so by step 2
 ofReal|F₁(w)| = ofReal(θ(Φ(w))) = (ofReal c^k)⁻¹·ofReal(θ(Φ(w)))·ofReal(c^k) ≤ (ofReal c^k)⁻¹·ofReal(θ(Φ(w)))·ofReal(J(w)),
 using ofReal c^k ∈ (0, ∞). Integrating (lintegral_mono_ae, lintegral_const_mul'):
 ∫⁻_D |F₁| ≤ (ofReal c^k)⁻¹ ∫⁻_D ofReal(θ∘Φ)·ofReal(J) = (ofReal c^k)⁻¹ ∫⁻_G ofReal(θ) dH ≤ (ofReal c^k)⁻¹ ∫⁻_G |θ| dH < ∞,
 where the equality is step 4. With step 5, ψ is L-integrable on Ω. This is the first conclusion.
7. (The representation.) Let f, A, α satisfy (i) and (ii). Put h(x) := θ(x)·(A(x)_#ξ(x))(α(f(x))) and X(w) := α(f(Φ(w)))(∂_0(f∘Φ)(w), …, ∂_{k−1}(f∘Φ)(w)).
 (7.1) By (ii) and the sibling signed_change_of_variables (same Φ and Ω, with A := G and h := h): ∫_G h dH = ∫_D h(Φ(w))·J(w) dw.
 (7.2) ψ·X = 1_D·(F₁·X). Hence ∫_Ω ψ·X dL = ∫_D F₁·X dL (integral_indicator₀ for L⌞Ω, and (L⌞Ω)⌞D = L⌞D).
 (7.3) For L⌞D-a.e. w, step 3 and (i) hold at w. For such w put x := Φ(w), v := ∂Φ(w) and γ := covectorPullback k (A(x)) (α(f(x))).
  - By definition of the push-forward, (A(x)_#ξ(x))(α(f(x))) = ξ(x)(γ).
  - Evaluating J(w)·ξ(x) = σ(w)·simpleNVector v at γ gives J(w)·ξ(x)(γ) = σ(w)·γ(v), and γ(v) = α(f(x))(A(x)v_0, …, A(x)v_{k−1}) (covectorPullback_apply).
  - By (i), fderiv ℝ (f∘Φ) w = A(x)∘DΦ(w) (HasFDerivAt.fderiv), so ∂_b(f∘Φ)(w) = A(x)(DΦ(w)e_b) = A(x)v_b.
  Hence h(x)·J(w) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(γ)·J(w) = θ(x)·σ(w)·α(f(x))(∂(f∘Φ)(w)) = F₁(w)·X(w).
 (7.4) By (7.3) and setIntegral_congr_ae₀ (D null-measurable), ∫_D h(Φ(w))·J(w) dw = ∫_D F₁·X dL. Combining with (7.1) and (7.2) gives ∫_G h dH = ∫_Ω ψ·X dL, the second conclusion. ∎
